incumbent.text: Decode every HTML character reference in each URI-valued attribute for the protocol-policy comparison only, leaving the serializer's entity-preserving output unchanged. Test numeric, named, mixed-case and malformed references plus allowed and relative controls.

hint: A Python sanitizer removes a plain disallowed scheme from a URI attribute, but the attribute policy compares an incompletely unescaped value while the serializer deliberately leaves character references unresolved. Baseline observation: plain javascript: is removed; hexadecimal, decimal, named-colon and named-tab variants of the same scheme remain in the emitted attribute; an allowed http value containing & and a relative path are emitted unchanged. The policy comparison currently uses a minimal unescape that handles only amp, lt and gt. The next step is to choose a repair scope and implement the smallest decoder that makes the policy see fully resolved characters without changing allowed output.
